evidence: Workbook Quality Checks row 43/check 42 requires a worse app never to outscore a better one; the internal row says to monitor this check. The frozen skill's quality-checks.md:172-173 specifically calls out gates that a stronger app fails. Public integration.md:5 says builders may choose routes, and behaviour.md:9 plus integration.md:7 require durable, shared exact saved fields, without requiring any particular save-response body. Yet constraints/judge.toml:27-32 makes its all_pass hard gate require a successful application WRITE response containing title, filename and source, even when a fresh independent server read confirms those exact fields. score.py:41-48 sets reward to zero whenever that gate fails; test.sh exits before the scored suite on gate failure. The 0.6 functional/0.2 polish/0.2 visual weights and 0.05 functional floor otherwise increase with dimension scores, but the extraneous response-shape prerequisite reverses the product ordering. This is a source-level counterexample; no full RewardKit ranking run or hash-bound runtime-evidence.json/raw-evidence-index.json was present for this frozen run, so empirical behavior remains unmeasured.
counterexample: App A fully implements the public editor, preview, durable shared library, conflict protection and history, but its successful Save returns 201 with only {id, revision}; a fresh independent GET returns the exact title, filename and source. It must fail cw_shared_saved_record solely because its write response does not echo fields and receives reward 0. App B uses the same compliant custom surface and a real shared backend, echoes those fields from Save, passes the authored JS Run gate, but omits most editing features. If it passes only typing/line join and HTML preview, its functional share is 2/30.5 = 0.0656, above the 0.05 floor, and it receives a positive reward (at least 0.0393 before polish/visual). Thus the materially worse B outscores A.
suggested_fix: Change the shared-record gate to require a successful save followed by exact identity/title/filename/source readback from an independent clean context and reload; accept a write response that returns only an identity or revision, while retaining the hard requirement for server-backed persistence.
